title: Open, but how open?
summary: An AI model can be available to use without being available to download, inspect or change. Learn what different kinds of access give you, and what to check before choosing a release.
takeaways: Open weights means the trained model files are available; permissions still depend on the licence.
Open-source AI also requires relevant code, training-data information and freedoms to change and share.
Check the exact release, computing requirements and operating responsibilities.

blocks.text: “Open” can describe several different things. A public chatbot lets you try a model, but that alone does not give you the files to run it. A downloadable release gives you more control over deployment, but may still leave its training process largely undocumented. Treat these as separate questions instead of a single yes-or-no label.

items.label: Open-source
items.title: Open-source AI: access plus freedoms
items.text: This guide uses the Open Source Initiative definition, which requires access needed to use, study, change and share the system.

layers.name: Use the model
layers.explanation: The definition includes freedom to use for any purpose.

layers.name: Run on your own computers
layers.explanation: Open licensing does not remove hardware requirements.

layers.name: Download weights
layers.explanation: Parameters must be available in the preferred form for modification.

layers.name: Training code
layers.explanation: Relevant code for training and running the system is required.

layers.name: Training-data information
layers.explanation: Sufficient detail is required; not every training example must be downloadable.

layers.name: Use, change and share rights
layers.explanation: The definition includes studying, modifying and sharing the system.

blocks.text: Under the Open Source Initiative’s definition, open-source AI must include weights, relevant code and sufficiently detailed training-data information, alongside the freedom to use, study, change and share it. The definition does not demand a freely downloadable copy of every training example. A publisher’s marketing label is not an independent certification.

Weights are numerical settings adjusted during training. They help determine how the model responds to a new question. Imagine a very large bank of dials: training adjusts them, and a weights download records the resulting settings. Those settings still need software and computing equipment to produce an answer.

blocks.text: Having those final settings does not automatically reveal every decision made during training. Code describes procedures; training-data information describes the material and preparation behind the learning process. A more complete release makes more of those choices available for inspection.

OpenAI’s gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b are downloadable models under Apache 2.0, with usage-policy documentation. They are separate from OpenAI’s hosted API models. This illustrates why it is better to classify an exact release than to call an entire company “open” or “closed.”

Claude Opus 5 appears in Anthropic’s hosted model catalogue. Access through a service lets a user submit requests while a provider operates the model; that offer does not supply public weights to run independently. Access to an assistant and possession of its model files are different arrangements.

NVIDIA publishes Nemotron 3 Ultra weights alongside development materials, including training datasets and recipes. Its model card lists OpenMDW-1.1 and substantial server requirements. This shows why examining the released materials is useful; this guide does not independently certify full compliance with the OSI definition.

Moonshot AI publishes Kimi K3 weights under a custom licence. Some commercial uses carry additional agreement or attribution conditions. Its size also makes clear that a public download is not automatically practical on a personal computer. Availability, permission and computing requirements need separate checks.

sections.title: Capability and openness answer different questions

blocks.text: “Can it work with pictures?” is a question about capability. “Can I download, inspect or change it?” is a question about access and rights. A text model may be either hosted or downloadable, and an image-capable model can have either arrangement. Do not infer one property from the other.

Similarly, downloadable weights do not establish that a model will be accurate, secure or inexpensive for your task. A useful evaluation asks whether it handles your examples reliably and whether the available software, licence and equipment support the way you intend to use it.

Running a model on infrastructure you control can let you choose where processing happens and how the system is adapted. Privacy still depends on the whole setup, including logs, connected tools and outside services. A local model connected to an external search tool still has an external data path.

The operator must budget for equipment, electricity, updates, access controls and people who maintain the system. Before adopting a release, ask who handles failures, how updates are tested, and how users report problems. Compare those responsibilities with the convenience and limits of a managed service.

items: Can I download this exact model’s weights?
